words.gloss: in the place where it prevails
is the one who truly restrains anger
in the place where it does not prevail

literal: In the place where it prevails, he who restrains, anger restrains; in the place where it does not prevail, if one restrains what? if one does not restrain what?
translation: He who restrains his anger where it can have effect is the one who truly restrains it. Where it has no effect, what does it matter whether he restrains it or not?
modern: தன் கோபம் செல்லுபடியாகும் இடத்தில் அதைக் கட்டுப்படுத்துபவனே கோபத்தைக் காப்பவன் ஆவான்; செல்லுபடியாகாத இடத்தில் அதைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தினால் என்ன, கட்டுப்படுத்தாவிட்டால் என்ன?
explanation: This couplet defines the true nature of anger management. Restraining anger is meaningful only when one has the power to express it and cause harm, such as towards subordinates or those who are weaker. In situations where one's anger has no power or effect, such as towards superiors or those who are stronger, it makes no difference whether one restrains it or lets it flare up, as it cannot affect the other person anyway. Therefore, true self-control is demonstrated only when one chooses not to be angry despite having the power to enforce it.
